audit_type: Multi-tier Dataset Leakage and Provenance Audit

tier_1_exact_duplicate_audit.conclusion: There are zero verbatim duplicate prompts between the training split and the held-out test split.

tier_2_near_duplicate_sampled_audit.scope: Stochastic sample comparison (500 test prompts vs 5,000 train prompts)
tier_2_near_duplicate_sampled_audit.important_limitation: This was a sampled check (500 prompts), NOT an exhaustive pairwise check of all 8,125 test prompts against all 37,913 train prompts (which would require ~308 million comparisons).

tier_3_source_level_split_provenance.analysis: ShieldLM was partitioned using random stratified sampling across classes, not by group-splitting across sources. Consequently, all 13 source repositories (e.g. alespalla/chatbot-instruction-prompts, spml/chatbot-prompt-injection) have examples distributed proportionally across train, validation, and test splits.
tier_3_source_level_split_provenance.evaluation_implication: Test prompts share stylistic provenance and domain distribution with training data. High benchmark test scores reflect in-distribution evaluation.

tier_4_independent_external_dataset_eval.status: Candidate for future out-of-distribution transfer benchmarking
tier_4_independent_external_dataset_eval.notes: External evaluation is required to measure true out-of-distribution robustness against unseen adversarial corpora.
